place.title: Place {ref} (0.96" OLED display)
place.text: Push the display's 4 header pins into column f: GND into hole {hole.gnd}, VCC into {hole.vcc}, SCL into {hole.scl} and SDA into {hole.sda}. The screen faces up and its board lies over the left half of the breadboard.
place.tip: Read the labels printed next to the pins: most of these boards are GND, VCC, SCL, SDA, but some have VCC first. Follow the labels, not the picture.

why: {ref} is a small 128 x 64 pixel screen (0.96 inch). The Pico talks to it over I2C: two wires, SDA (data) and SCL (clock), shared by everything on the bus. It runs on 3.3 V here so its data lines stay at the Pico's 3.3 V.

wire.i2c_sda: {pin} is the I2C{bus} data line (SDA): the Pico sends the pixels to {ref} on this wire.
